audit.whatIsWrong: Row 4 (Level 6) contradicts itself across layers: full phases[4].side reads "Diana" while content win[4] reads "Aurora". The remaining six full sides read "Skill" against content/packet "Aurora", and the packet's all-Aurora chart sits against a 49.1% win rate over 1226 games with the page rated TRICKY 7/10.
audit.why: Level 6 belongs to Diana and the kit says why: Moonfall reveals and draws in everything within 475 and crashes after a delay, and it arrives on a champion who already gets Lunar Rush for free onto any Moonlight-marked target. A 49.1% win rate does not support Aurora owning all seven rows, and the full layer's 7/10 rating on that row is the considered verdict. So win[4] moves to Diana to match phases[4].side.
audit.corrected: win[4] set to Diana, paired with phases[4].side which already reads Diana; phases[4].why and whys[4] both rewritten in the same proposal to argue Diana at 6. The six "Skill" rows are LEFT ALONE — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes said "Luden's makes the rotation half a bar", phases[3].why claimed "three-spell spirit stacks proc your passive haste", and content whys[4]/spikes[2] described first-item timings as "even" without naming what actually changes.
audit.why: Aurora's passive heals, it grants no haste. "Half a bar" has no source. The real spike structure is: full kit at 3; Diana's spike at 6 with Moonfall; and at first item the thing that matters is whether Pale Cascade (15s at rank 1) is up to absorb the opening burst.
audit.corrected: Spikes rebuilt on Moonfall at 6 and on forcing Pale Cascade out before committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was named only vaguely ("Moonlight marks reset her dash") and never with the number, while four separate fabrications were stated as fact: (a) Crescent Strike slows — it does not, it applies Moonlight and reveals non-stealthed targets for 3 seconds, and the page tells the reader to "dodge the slow" (early) and that she wants to "slow you before jumping in" (wants.foe[0]); (b) Moonfall "empowers her next auto" (mid) — Riot's R text has no auto-attack empower, it is a reveal, a draw-in, a slow and a delayed crash; (c) Between Worlds "phases you out of the pull" (whys[3], spikes[1], mid, late, wants.you[2]) — R is a leap with a slowing zone and a cross-zone teleport, with no untargetability in the text; (d) Crescent Strike "bounces off minions/monsters" (wants.you[1]) — it is an arc, not a bounce. Pale Cascade's shield is never mentioned once.
audit.why: Riot's E text is explicit: "Lunar Rush has no cooldown when used to dash to an enemy afflicted with Moonlight." So the arc is the dive. Unmarked, that dash is 22/20/18/16/14 — 22 seconds at rank 1 — and Diana has no other way to close 900. The same text also gives a real, unstated interaction: any Moonlight-marked enemy works, including a minion, so a Q that clips the melee line beside you is a free dash onto that minion.
audit.corrected: Every field now runs on mark-then-free-dash, the 22s unmarked cooldown, Pale Cascade's 15s shield being forced out before you commit, and Moonfall's reveal/pull/delayed crash at 475. The four fabrications are removed rather than restated.
sources: diana kit Q/W/E/R text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things in the text were never used: Lunar Rush works off a marked MINION, and Moonfall reveals.
audit.why: Riot's E text says Lunar Rush dashes to "an enemy" afflicted with Moonlight and has no cooldown doing so, and adds that all other enemies lose the debuff regardless. Riot's R text opens "reveals and draws in all nearby enemies" — that reveal matters against a champion whose escape is an invisibility leap.
audit.corrected: Marked-minion dash added to early and wants.you[1]; Moonfall's reveal added to dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Diana was called he/his throughout the full layer: tldr ("He dives"), winCon ("his failed timers", "poke he can't return"), tradeGood ("he answered"), tradeBad ("his engage"), ahead ("hop his answers"), loading ("his engage"), dosFull[0].t ("his engage"), dosFull[2].t ("his roams"), report[9].t ("His answer goes first").
audit.why: champ-gender lists diana as female; the owner is "you", so every third-person pronoun on this page is Diana.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and both spikes[0] and wants.you[0] told the reader to punish Crescent Strike's "long cooldown" — it is 8s at rank 1 and 6s maxed.
audit.why: The long cooldown in this matchup is Lunar Rush at 22s when it is not refunded by a mark, and Moonfall at 100s. Calling an 8-second Q a long cooldown teaches the wrong window.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rebuilt with 8s/6s Q, 22s unmarked E, 15s W; the punish window moved to the dash.

edits.before: Diana telegraphs Crescent Strike with a slow arcing animation, so if you track her cast and dash through or around it with E you dodge the slow and immediately punish her long cooldown with your own Q. Watch the wave too: a Q that clips a minion beside you gives her a free dash onto that minion, so do not stand shoulder to shoulder with the melee line.

edits.before: Level 6 is when Diana threatens her real all-in: Moonfall pulls you in and empowers her next auto, but Between Worlds lets you phase away mid-pull and completely deny the follow-up damage. Keep baiting her Q before she reaches level 6 threat range so she's forced to all-in without her slow secured.
edits.after: Level 6 is her level, not yours. Moonfall reveals and draws in everyone within 475, slows them, then crashes down after a short delay — there is no auto-attack empower in it, and there is no phasing out of it either; Between Worlds is a leap, and the pull happens first. The answer is upstream: she has to land Crescent Strike to make Lunar Rush free, so hold W for the dash arriving rather than for the arc, and stay off the mark.

edits.before: Your item spikes track evenly with hers heading into the late game, so the matchup stays about equal on raw damage — the real edge is still your Between Worlds phase, which voids her Q-into-R chain lockdown in extended fights. edits.after: Late, Moonfall is the fight: it draws in everything inside 475 and hits harder for each extra champion pulled, so the single biggest thing you control is not standing next to a teammate when she jumps. Pale Cascade shields the opening burst, so open with Q and the recast to strip it, then commit. Bait, then combo.

notes: PACKET SUSPECTNAMES IS A FALSE POSITIVE: "Land Crescent Strike" in wants.foe[0] is the correct Q name. The real defect in that string was the claim that it SLOWS — it does not; it applies Moonlight and reveals non-stealthed targets for 3 seconds. Diana's only slow is on Moonfall. SIX CHART ROWS LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY: full phases[0..3,5,6].side all read "Skill" while content win[] and the packet chart read "Aurora" on those rows. I did not flip them, because the packet's all-Aurora chart sits against a 49.1% win rate over 1226 games and a 7/10 difficulty rating — I cannot tell from the kits which of the two is right, and per the chart rule a stale row beats a row I invented. Only row 4 is resolved, because there the two layers openly contradict each other and Moonfall at 6 grounds the verdict. RATING SEMANTICS: I read phases[N].rating as the strength of the named side's edge, because phases[4] carries "Diana" with 7/10 while contested rows carry 5-6/10. On that reading no rating needed to move here. If the field actually means Aurora-favourability, phases[4] is already wrong on disk and this row needs a second look. UNVERIFIED AND NOT WRITTEN: whether Crescent Strike's reveal strips Aurora's W invisibility (the kit's derived flag says revealsStealth, but Riot's text reads "revealing them if they are not stealthed", which points the other way — I stated only Moonfall's reveal, which the R text gives outright); whether Aurora's R leap can be used while being drawn in by Moonfall; and whether tenacity or Cleanse shortens the Moonfall slow.
